changes: New store listings, including ones found on other stores, get their first price within minutes instead of waiting for the store's next scheduled check.
Other stores now searches Blade HQ regularly and shows its sale prices; KnifeCenter was removed because it blocks whole networks.
Other stores now searches Amazon at a delivery ZIP you can set, finds your knives there, and only adds a listing when its page shows your knife's exact model number.
The Checks per hour chart on Price Drops now has a colour legend showing what each bar colour means.
Price comparisons now say "Regular price" instead of "You paid", since many knives in a collection were added rather than bought.
Supervisor activity now has its own tab on Price Drops, with a run timeline and a table of each run's actions.
Price monitoring now finds your knives on Amazon, Blade HQ and KnifeCenter, and keeps searching after a store has a few failed page loads.
Confirm stock changes in the price tests added before #604.
Set a target price or mute a knife, snooze price messages or mute a store for a while, dismiss all price messages at once, and get desktop notifications for drops and restocks.
Export a knife's store price history, or every knife's, to a CSV file from the Market tab or the Price Drops page.
Price monitoring can ignore sold-out official sites, look for your knives on Blade HQ and KnifeCenter as well as Amazon, and link each price drop to the store where it happened.
Collection cards, the table and Smart Collections can now show and filter by each knife's market price: dropped, back in stock, out of stock, or below what you paid.
Price monitoring checks long out-of-stock pages once a day, suggests pausing listings that seem gone, adds per-store actions in Settings and shows live progress for Check all.
Price Drops can now be searched, filtered by store, sorted and grouped by knife, shows restocks, out-of-stock age and below-what-you-paid listings, and works on phones.
Price Drops uses one set of colours for drops, increases, stock and problems in every style, and blocked stores get a clear Solve button.
The Market tab and Price Drops panel now show lowest and highest prices, change markers on the chart, each store's check history, and let you manage a knife's stores without edit mode.
Stock alerts now wait for a second check to confirm the change, so a store briefly showing the wrong stock no longer sends false "Back in stock" or "Out of stock" alerts.
AI clients connected through MCP can now read price drops, history and problems, and manage a knife's store URLs and Check now.
Price Drops now ignores price moves smaller than your Minimum change, marks prices that go back and forth as Fluctuating, and explains when a store shows a different currency than you paid in.
Old Cloudflare storage credentials left in early vaults are now deleted, so new backups no longer contain them.

Price Drops reads more accurately: small price moves keep a decimal, overdue checks say so, out-of-stock is counted separately, times follow your 12/24-hour setting, and Solve in browser is only offered where its window can open.
AI price monitoring through OpenCode Go asks models to answer without reasoning, so runs no longer fail with an empty answer.
Choose how much AI price monitoring may use: Limited with daily request and token caps (the default), or Unlimited for models that can run all day.

An optional AI supervisor reviews all price monitoring and decides what to check first, which failing pages to retry with AI, and which gone pages to pause; it can only observe or act within fixed limits.
With AI connected, BladeVault can confirm price changes against the store page before notifying you, spot-check page readings in Unlimited mode, and post a short daily price summary in the Inbox.
Price Drops shows the AI supervisor: its latest summary, coverage, what still needs you, and a feed of every action it took, with a switch between Off, Observe and Act.
AI price reading now works with large reasoning models such as GLM: it reads most of the product page, gets enough time and answer room, and Settings shows what AI did in the last 24 hours.
Stores whose product pages include review widgets, such as Civivi, are no longer mistaken for bot checks, and Solve in browser's Done now saves for them.
Price monitoring now checks every store's US edition in US dollars, even when your IP is in another country.
Other stores now finds knives on Amazon, and the AI advisor works, when the AI model is a reasoning model that used to return empty answers.
Price monitoring's AI is harder to trick with text on store pages: it never follows links off a store, never touches sign-in forms, and only pauses products whose page is really gone.
Update CLAUDE.md with tooling and server details.
Price monitoring can now let AI find your monitored knives on Amazon, confirm the listing, and watch its price alongside the knife's own store.
Connect BladeVault to Claude Desktop with one click from Settings → AI / MCP.
Track store prices for knives in your collection: BladeVault checks them gently in the background and shows drops, increases and stock changes on a new Price Drops page and in your Inbox.

When AI assistance is on, BladeVault works through cookie banners, pop-ups and variant pickers to read prices, and you can pass a store's bot check yourself with Solve in browser from Price Drops or the Inbox.
Google Drive backups now say when they finish or fail, failed backups stay in the Inbox until fixed, and the Inbox has All, Maintenance and System tabs.
Choose an exact date when rescheduling a care job from the Maintenance timeline.

Price alert Minimum change is now a single percentage field: price changes smaller than it don't notify.

Studio blends photo backgrounds into the cards in gallery tiles, focus mode, and Quick Look, in both light and dark modes.
Boker imports read the original photo URLs from product galleries, so every gallery image is imported in order without unrelated brand logos.
Modern Collection, Insights, and Studio start higher on screen now that their extra header rows are gone. Smart Collection controls moved into the Collection toolbar.
Collection additions in Modern Insights always covers the last 12 calendar months, including the current month, without a date-range selector.

Poikilo Blade pages load fully before importing, so the brand, price, lock, and gallery are captured instead of footer text and unrelated images. Protected gallery photos download with the required referrer.

Zero Tolerance imports wait for the dynamic product content and prefer the complete description and explicitly labeled specifications, skipping recommendation images, video thumbnails, and placeholder lock values.
Studio’s repeated workspace row is gone, and Focus mode is now an icon button in the workspace header.

A new Modern appearance refreshes Collection, Compare, and Logs with a shared header and search, a quieter sidebar, and inline log details. The original Current theme stays the default.
Studio is a new visual library with randomized layouts for browsing by model family, plus filters, sorting, quick actions, and a focus mode for single-knife viewing.
Modern Collection columns can be shown, hidden, dragged into a new order, and resized, with every choice remembered across reloads.
Select knives directly from the modern Collection list to bulk edit, add to Compare, pin, or delete them.
Insights was rebuilt as Collection pulse, combining collection growth, field coverage, maker and steel mix, blade length versus weight, and recent additions with links back to the records.
Settings → Appearance → Start page lets BladeVault open on Insights, Studio, or Collection at launch.
Choose Current or Modern in Settings → Appearance. More theme options are on the way.
Model names can be bulk edited across several knives at once.
Product imports preserve the complete scraped details and screenshots instead of trimming them.
Standard field extraction was improved across supported retailers.
The Add and Update product views gained a full-width preview you can resize while reviewing an import.
The interactive import browser clears popup overlays, so retailer pages that block the normal importer stay usable.
Vosteed imports separate their specifications more reliably and flag conflicting values from the source page.
Compare search now accepts model numbers.
Knives can be marked as sold, so a collection can track what has left the shelf as well as what is still on it.
Pasted product links are imported one at a time, in order, so a long list no longer races ahead of itself.
Batch scraping skips products already saved from the same source URL instead of creating a duplicate record.
Cloud backup uploads and restores are no longer speed-limited, so large vaults move noticeably faster.
A browser-only preview of BladeVault now runs on free static hosting at bladevault.tkweb.dev, starting from an empty collection with session-only changes.

Cloud restores now run on the local server, so switching pages or reloading no longer cancels a restore that has already started. You can keep browsing the current vault while the backup downloads and validates.
Edits and automatic backups pause while a restore is prepared, then the restored vault installs and open views and images refresh. Progress stays quiet, with no completion popup.
Responsive layouts and collection cards were polished for consistent spacing.
Cloud backups run quietly in the background and continue across page navigation and browser reloads. Settings shows a calm status with the last successful backup.
The selected knife drawer gained Pin / Unpin and Edit actions alongside Open full page and Add to compare.
The Data completeness page was redesigned to make reviewing and filling in missing details easier.
Insight detail pages use unified full-width responsive layouts, and desktop typography and settings layouts were polished for large and 4K displays.
Redundant explanatory copy was removed from the interface.
Completeness now guides you through cleaning up incomplete collection records.
Measurements are corrected and populated fields are preserved when importing products.
Set an optional local vault password in Settings → App lock. The lock is off by default and asks for your password on the next app launch or browser session.
Change or remove the password from Settings, or use Lock now to lock the current session. Cloud Backup sign-in remains separate.
Maker Mix and Lock Types tooltips stay visible without being clipped by their charts.
Self-hosted Docker pages load more efficiently, and Insights charts load as they approach the visible part of the page.
New URL imports capture a full-page screenshot of the source webpage alongside the product images.
Open captured pages in a scrollable viewer with source and download actions. Capture or replace a screenshot from Edit → Images.
Capture source pages for older items from Settings. Local and cloud backups include the saved screenshots.

Gallery controls, thumbnail borders, and long tooltip text received a focused visual polish pass.
